name: TBO TEK Ltd
title: TBO TEK Ltd - 544174 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: TBO Tek Q4 FY26 grew YoY on top and bottom line despite Middle East war; Q1 FY27 guided better than Q4 and last year, with no figures given.
summary.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 showed YoY growth in revenue and profit despite the war that began at end-February 2026, which hit the Middle East and Israel, TBO's largest source markets. January and February showed strong operating leverage, margin expansion and EBITDA growth YoY, but March was a washout and erased the quarter-level leverage. Management expects Q1 FY27 to beat Q4 and last year on both GTV and gross profit, while declining to quantify it. Cash flow from operations was negative in FY26, which management attributed mainly to timing items (Brazil anticipation discontinuation, war-related receivable delays, PLB payouts and deposits classified as working capital) and expects reversion to over 100% cash conversion by year-end.

financial_highlights.value: Rs. 110 crore (as cited by analyst; company did not dispute)
financial_highlights.change: Management did not give YoY figure on the call; growth stated only qualitatively
Expected to taper slightly in FY27

financial_highlights.value: ~4-5% YoY for full year, primarily hotel GTV
financial_highlights.change: Management does not report constant currency

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow and FCF FY26
financial_highlights.change: Management attributes to timing; FY25 CFO/PAT ~90% per analyst

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Hotel GTV is about 50:50 retail vs API by GTV, with retail higher on gross profit; hotels are higher-margin and expected to grow faster than air GTV. Hotel GTV carries most of the FX benefit.

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: Air GTV is back to about Rs. 3,400 crore on an organic basis per analyst; management says Q1 air trajectory is a shade better than Q4.

segments.name: Classic Vacations / North America
segments.commentary: Management views Classic and TBO North America as one business; expects significant YoY growth but declined to quantify. Integration is about halfway; target completion by end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: LATAM (Brazil)
segments.commentary: Management expects moderate growth in FY27 given currency and IOF tax headwinds; Brazil is not among top three source markets.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: Growing from a small base, led by Australia after investment; some APAC-based API partners add growth. Price-competitive market.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 GTV and gross profit expected to grow YoY and QoQ, assuming no change in geopolitical status quo; no figures given.
Q1 FY27 EBITDA expected to grow in USD terms YoY and vs Q4; management declined to comment further.
SG&A growth to taper slightly from ~16%; top line to grow faster than SG&A, with operating leverage and margin expansion as the aim.
Long-term aspiration to grow early-to-mid 20s% per year; management says unless normalcy weakens, growth should stay in that range.
Cash flow conversion expected to return to over 100% of EBITDA/PAT by end of FY27, per management; timing items to resolve after Q2.
Brazil anticipation loss expected to fade after Q2 FY27 as receivables recover; ETR of 18% to 18.5%.
capex_capacity: Tech costs capitalised only for new features and products; amortisation period 3 to 5 years.
Classic platform migration underway; integration targeted to complete by end of calendar 2026.
Classic supply access: TBO connectivity established, but only high-curation luxury hotel supply opened to Classic so far.
Debt: five-year facility with one-year moratorium; repayments start Q3 FY27 and run four more years.
demand_pricing: Middle East and Israel saw sharp drops; management says Middle East bookings in April-May are slightly better than 30-40% below pre-war, but still well below normal in volume terms; in pockets volumes match pre-war levels.
Demand is shifting to Europe and Asia Pacific; Japan popular with HNIs, ultra-HNI still travelling to Europe.
Airfares higher and some airline capacity cut (domestic and international), though management views part of the cuts as temporary.
Take rate: management says no downward pressure currently, intends to hold current levels and not raise them.
Expedia: management says it is not a direct competitor in most of TBO's growth markets; B2B growing faster than B2C industry-wide.
Cancellations exceeded bookings for some pockets (Israel) during March; enterprise-level sales never negative for a day.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any reason for Q4's strong hotels and ancillary growth despite geopolitical shocks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to market-development investment starting January 2025, with new travel agents becoming productive after 6-9 months; some large partners went live in Q4. Majority of growth is market share gain.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA-to-GTV (stable at ~1% over three years) rise in FY27 as SG&A growth tapers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management considers it a reasonable assumption, driven by SG&A tapering and mix shift toward higher-margin hotels.

qa_highlights.question: How much EBITDA was lost in March due to the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; said costs were unchanged and incremental GTV would have largely flowed to the bottom line, a significant loss.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital drivers and when do cash flows normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were PLB payouts (Jan-Dec for hotels, April-March for air), delayed Middle East collections around Eid, bank deposits over 12 months classified in working capital, and Brazil anticipation reversal; expected to normalise by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How is management handling competitive pressure on take rates?
qa_highlights.answer: No downward pressure today; management intends to hold take rates at current levels and not raise them, as TBO operates an aggregation model.

qa_highlights.question: Will the rupee depreciation help GTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year YoY FX impact estimated at 4-5%, primarily on hotel GTV. Management will consider constant-currency reporting after an analyst suggestion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SG&A plan for Classic and North America?
qa_highlights.answer: Early days; platform migration underway. Management will look at combined TBO North America and Classic cost base before commenting on dollar cost reduction.

risks_watch: Middle East and Israel recovery pace; management says two quarters of normalcy are needed before judging the growth reset.
Working capital and cash conversion: FY26 CFO and FCF negative; watch if conversion returns above 100% by FY27 year-end.
Airline capacity cuts and higher airfares may reduce ticket volumes for the same GTV, especially in summer season (Q2).
Competitive take-rate pressure from global peers; management currently sees none.
Classic integration (about halfway) and SG&A efficiency uncertain; no quantified targets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term strategy and recovery in non-war markets, but cautious and non-quantitative on Q1 FY27, Middle East timing and Classic cost benefits; management repeatedly declined to give numbers.
key_quotes: we were still able to demonstrate growth both on the top line and the bottom line.
we would still expect Q1 to be better than Q4, and we would also expect Q1 to be better than same period last year.
the aspiration as we have always talked about is to grow in that range right at least , I will not say mid-to-high 20s but early -to-mid 20s .
We absolutely intend to maintain them at the current levels.

growth.why: Management guides Q1 FY27 GTV and gross profit better than Q4 and last year (unquantified), and holds a long-term aspiration of early-to-mid 20s% growth, backed by demand recovery, SG&A operating leverage and Classic/NA integration rather than specific capacity or orders.
